newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cautious Euro-bourses take heart from Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cautious Euro-bourses take heart from Wall St.

text.p: European stock and bond markets, reacting to Wall Street's best one-day rally for three weeks, clawed back some of their losses on Tuesday.
The dollar held firm in early trade but below a 37-month high of 1.7350 marks set overnight, while bond markets ticked higher.
Wall Street's 60 point rise, following Friday's 148 point plunge, drove European bourses although investors continued to fret at the prospect of higher interest rates.

"The opening spike was inevitable after the Dow's rally," the head of trading at a large brokerage in London said. "But unless we see some volume behind the move, it won't last -- and I'm not looking for any brave buying just yet."
Dealers expected investors to remain cautious ahead of U.S. consumer price (CPI) inflation numbers, due at 1230 GMT.

Stocks on both sides of the Atlantic suffered badly after strong U.S. wholesale figures last Friday, and similarly strong retail numbers would underline fears that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again next month.

"The market is pricing in higher U.S. rates which will only be reinforced by a strong number today," said a German foreign exchange dealer. "But a soft number won't do much damage to the dollar given the Fed's pre-emptive monetary policy. This will keep the rate hike talk ticking over for a while."

The market reaction to Wall Street displayed by the major European bourses was reflected amongst second-tier markets too. Amsterdam's AEX index was showing gains of 1.24 percent by 0915, while Milan's MIBTEL was up 1.34 percent.
Among the majors, Frankfurt rebounded the best after being the biggest loser on Monday.
The 30-share DAX benchmark was nearly 1.5 percent up at 3,328 by mid-morning.
Dealers were focusing on the U.S. price data, but some traders said the German market was still underpinned by domestic fundamentals, including the weaker mark.
The shares of carmakers were at the forefront, with Volkswagen AG, BMW AG and Daimler all posting gains based on support from the dollar at 1.73 marks.
London dealers also predicted investors would remain cautious ahead of the U.S. figures, although the FTSE 100 index also pushed modestly higher in early trade.
The head of trading at a major investment bank said the Wall Street rally had not been convincing. "The volume was low and the rally was confirmed by buying in second-line stocks."
LucasVarity Plc was up 2-1/2p to 203p after the car components group compensated for a dividend cut with a three percent share buy-back.
Smith & Nephew Plc added 3p to 181-1/2 after the healthcare company said clinical trials of one of its products had shown favourable results.
French shares started one percent higher on the back of the firmer dollar and gains on Wall Street, but later trimmed their gains to about 0.55 percent as caution took hold.
LVMH was 4.51 percent higher at 1,345 francs after it reproted a big rise in first quarter sales. DIOR, up 3.44 percent at 841 franc, followed suit.

On the foreign exchange market, the prospect of higher U.S. rates was the dominating factor behind the dollar's strength and was reflected in a widening of the yield gap between U.S. and German 10-year bonds.
The dollar was quoted at 1.7310 marks and 126.20 yen after ending at 1.7228 marks and 126.45 yen in late trading in Europe on Monday.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's comment on Monday that U.S. dollar policy was unchanged caused little surprise.

"The basic thing is there is no policy opposition to the rising dollar, it still has another couple of pfennigs to go before raising (strong dollar) policy risk," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN-Amro in London.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7310 marks and 126.20 yen after ending at 1.7228 marks and 126.45 yen in late trading in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0915 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 9.1 points, or 0.21 percent, at 4,260.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 14.40 points, or 0.56 percent, at 2,580.53.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 48.96 points, or 1.49 percent, at 3,328.86
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted easier at $345.75 versus $346.55 at Monday's close in London. Silver was one cent easier at $4.72.
